slides.title: Eukaryotes vs Prokaryotes
slides.text: Eukaryotic cells (plant and animal) contain genetic material enclosed in a nucleus. Prokaryotic cells (bacterial) are much smaller and do not have a nucleus. Genetic material is a single DNA loop plus plasmids.

slides.title: Organelle Functions: Boundaries & Control
slides.text: The Nucleus (Eukaryotes) Function: Contains the genetic material (packaged as chromosomes) that controls the activities of the cell. Plasmids (Prokaryotes) Function: Small, circular rings of extra DNA found in bacteria, separate from the main genetic loop. Cell Membrane (All Cells) Function: Contains receptor molecules and provides a selective barrier to control which molecules enter and exit the cell.

slides.title: Specialised Cells Overview
slides.text: As organisms develop, cells differentiate to form specialised cells with specific functions. Animal examples: Sperm cell (reproduction), Nerve cell (conduction), Muscle cell (contraction). Plant examples: Root hair cell (water absorption), Xylem (water transport), Phloem (food transport).
